answer: Agents buying a summit weather model to predict how a zephyr affects vine growth fetch it from untrusted peers. The buyer pins the publisher-signed Merkle root in its purchase order and accepts each chunk only with a valid inclusion proof under that root. A thousand fake serving identities cannot substitute poisoned chunks by agreeing on them: acceptance depends on hashes, not peer votes. This resists sybil content substitution, assuming a trusted publisher and secure hashes; peers can still withhold data.
